title: Spin-precession visualizer
question: How do signed gamma/(2 pi), field magnitude, and time determine signed cyclic frequency, angular frequency, and phase in the declared model?
predictionPrompt: Under phi = -omega t with B along positive z, predict clockwise or counterclockwise rotation for the selected signed gamma; keep omega = 2 pi f explicit.
sourceRevision: CODATA 2022 adjustment; OpenStax University Physics Volume 3, 2016 web edition accessed 2026-07-27; Tour contract 2026-07-26
sourceLocator: Signed free-particle gamma/(2 pi) values; OpenStax sections 8.2-8.3; Chapter 9 moment-field limits
caveats: The unit-circle marker is phase-model output, not an observed classical spin trajectory.
No relaxation, shielding, material response, environmental coupling, or detector measurement is represented.

numericalMethod.name: Bounded signed precession phase evaluation
numericalMethod.description: Evaluates signed cyclic and angular frequencies, period, phase, and 2-128 deterministic unit-circle samples.

modelComponents.label: Signed free-particle cyclic gyromagnetic ratios
modelComponents.description: Supplies signed gamma/(2 pi) in Hz per tesla for electron, free proton, and negative muon.

attribution.sourceLocator: gamma/(2 pi) entries for electron, free proton, and negative muon
caveats: The ratios are model inputs; their uncertainties are not propagated.

modelComponents.label: Moment-field phase model
modelComponents.description: Uses mu = gamma S and H = -mu dot B with phi = -omega t to evolve transverse phase in a static uniform field along positive z.

attribution.sourceRevision: OpenStax University Physics Volume 3, 2016 web edition accessed 2026-07-27; Tour contract 2026-07-26
attribution.sourceLocator: OpenStax sections 8.2-8.3; Deep curriculum Chapter 9 technical extension
caveats: The activity does not derive gamma from a microscopic particle model.

modelComponents.label: Signed phase and unit-circle projection
modelComponents.description: Converts cyclic to angular frequency exactly once, applies phi = -omega t, and projects signed phase to x=cos(phi), y=sin(phi).

attribution.sourceLocator: Frequency, phase, period, and sample output definitions
caveats: The coordinates are visualization state, not detector samples.

equations: mu = gamma S; H = -mu dot B
f = (gamma/(2 pi)) B; omega = 2 pi f = gamma B
phi(t) = -omega t; phaseCycles = -f * t; T = 1/|f|; x = cos(phi); y = sin(phi)
assumptions: A static uniform magnetic field points along positive z and the control supplies its positive magnitude from 10^-6 through 20 T.
The selected catalog ratio is the signed free-particle gamma/(2 pi), not angular gamma and not a shielded material value.
The particle starts at phase zero and uses phi=-omega t, x=cos(phi), y=sin(phi).
Time is bounded from 0 through 10 s and sample count from 2 through 128 including both endpoints.
Relaxation, shielding, field gradients, interactions, material response, detector signals, and uncertainty are omitted.

controls.label: Free particle
controls.description: Selects one engine catalog particle and its signed cyclic gamma/(2 pi) value.
controls.playfulPrompt: Switch sign and watch the declared phase convention reverse direction.

controls.label: Magnetic field magnitude
controls.description: Sets a positive static uniform field magnitude along the declared positive z axis.
controls.playfulPrompt: Double the field and predict both frequency magnitudes.

controls.label: Elapsed model time
controls.description: Sets elapsed phase-evolution time within the engine bound.
controls.playfulPrompt: Advance model time without calling the marker a detector trace.

controls.label: Phase sample count
controls.description: Sets the deterministic table and unit-circle sample count, including both time endpoints.
controls.playfulPrompt: Change display resolution without changing the endpoint phase.

presets.label: Free proton at 1 T
presets.description: Maps to the engine's conventional free-proton 1 T state for 1 microsecond; it is not a material-specific nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) line.
presets.inspectionPrompt: Convert about 42.58 MHz to angular frequency with one explicit factor 2 pi.

presets.label: Free proton at 3 T
presets.description: Maps to the engine's conventional free-proton 3 T state for 1 microsecond without shielding or material response.
presets.inspectionPrompt: Predict the factor-of-three change in f and omega before revealing it.

presets.label: Electron reference at 0.34 T
presets.description: Maps to the engine electron resonance reference state for 1 nanosecond; no material g-tensor is modeled.
presets.inspectionPrompt: Predict the negative signed frequencies and counterclockwise marker under phi = -omega t.

presets.label: Earth-ish free-proton field
presets.description: Uses a representative 50 microtesla input for 1 millisecond, not a local geomagnetic measurement.
presets.inspectionPrompt: Keep the field labeled as a conventional input rather than observed data.

outputSchema.label: Signed gamma divided by 2 pi
outputSchema.description: Selected signed free-particle cyclic gyromagnetic ratio; not angular gamma.

outputSchema.label: Signed cyclic frequency
outputSchema.description: f = (gamma/(2 pi))B retaining the catalog sign.

outputSchema.label: Cyclic frequency magnitude
outputSchema.description: Absolute value |f| used for the positive reciprocal period.

outputSchema.label: Signed angular frequency
outputSchema.description: omega = 2 pi f with sign retained and the conversion applied exactly once.

outputSchema.label: Angular frequency magnitude
outputSchema.description: Absolute value |omega| reported separately from signed angular frequency.

outputSchema.label: Signed endpoint phase
outputSchema.description: Negative omega times selected elapsed model time: phi = -omega t.

outputSchema.label: Signed endpoint cycles
outputSchema.description: Negative signed cyclic frequency times selected elapsed model time: phaseCycles = -f * t, linked to phaseRadians by 2 pi.

outputSchema.label: Rotation sense
outputSchema.description: Clockwise for positive omega and counterclockwise for negative omega under phi = -omega t in the stated x-y projection.

comparison.incompatibleBehavior: Render parallel model findings without merging phases or calculating measurement residuals when compatibility keys differ.

visualization.description: Shows a bounded unit-circle phase marker, rotation-sense label, signed cyclic frequency, signed angular frequency, and positive period.

alternatives.description: A sentence states particle, field input, signed gamma/(2 pi), signed f, signed omega, positive period, endpoint phase, rotation convention, and omitted physics.
A table lists 2-128 deterministic samples with index, model time, signed phase, x, and y, including both endpoints.

visualization.reducedMotionBehavior: Render the endpoint marker, direction label, and complete sample table immediately without animated rotation.

finding.changed: At runtime, particle sign sets rotation sense, field scales both frequencies linearly, time sets endpoint phase, and sample count changes only visualization resolution.
finding.cause: The moment-field phase model multiplies signed gamma/(2 pi) by positive B, converts cyclic to angular frequency with exactly one factor 2 pi, and applies the declared phase sign phi = -omega t.
finding.equation: mu = gamma S; H = -mu dot B; f = (gamma/(2 pi))B; omega = 2 pi f; phi = -omega t; phaseCycles = -f * t
assumptions: Static uniform field along positive z with positive magnitude
Signed free-particle cyclic gamma/(2 pi) catalog input
Initial phase zero with phi=-omega t and x=cos(phi), y=sin(phi)
finding.establishes: For an evaluated state, the declared model computes signed cyclic and angular frequencies, positive period, signed phase, rotation sense, and bounded visualization samples.
finding.doesNotEstablish: An observed resonance, relaxation, shielding, material or composite response, detector signal, fitted uncertainty, or validation of a magnetic-moment or geometric particle theory.
finding.sourceRevision: CODATA 2022; OpenStax University Physics Volume 3, 2016 web edition accessed 2026-07-27; Tour contract 2026-07-26
finding.sourceLocator: Spin precession equations, controls, outputs, OpenStax sections 8.2-8.3, and Chapter 9 limits
caveats: Signed cyclic and angular frequencies encode rotation sense only after applying the stated axis and phi=-omega t phase convention.
The period uses magnitude and remains positive.
No T1/T2 relaxation, shielding, anisotropic response, material response, field gradient, interaction, or detector model is included.
